sources.entry: Sshwifty - Sshwifty is a SSH and Telnet connector made for the Web. (Demo) AGPL-3.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Sshwifty is a web-based SSH and Telnet client that lets you reach SSH and Telnet servers directly from a browser.
summary.what_it_does: Sshwifty serves a web interface from a Go backend that connects to remote SSH and Telnet hosts on the user's behalf, so the terminal runs in the browser. It can be installed from prebuilt executables, a Docker image (niruix/sshwifty), or built from source with npm and Go. Configuration is via a JSON file or environment variables, covering listen address and port, TLS certificate files, a shared access password, timeouts, and an optional SOCKS5 proxy for outbound connections. Operators can define "Presets" with host, type, and form fields so users don't have to type connection details, and can restrict connections to presets only. Server-side Hooks can run external commands before a connection is made, and it can show a server message on the home page. The README notes that a reverse proxy is the usual place to terminate TLS and that HTTPS is needed for the browser crypto features it relies on.
use_cases: access SSH servers from a web browser
browser-based Telnet access to legacy devices
shared web terminal for a team
jump-host style access behind a reverse proxy
preset connection bookmarks for common servers
notable: Web-based SSH and Telnet client with no client-side install
Server-side Hooks that run external processes before connecting, with a timeout
Presets define connection targets and fields, with optional locked metadata sourced from files or environment variables
Optional SOCKS5 proxy for outbound connections
Configurable via JSON file or environment variables, with multiple HTTP listeners in file mode
caveats: Maintenance-only project: the author states new features are not accepted and pull requests are not wanted
Prebuilt executables are not tested by the authors; the Homebrew formula is third-party and unsupported
Requires accurate clocks on client and server and a secure context (HTTPS) for the wire protocol; subpath hosting is unsupported
